reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Open umbilical hernia repair in Child B (MELD 16) alcohol associated cirrhosis. The chart says abstinent since 2024, but PEth 286 in August and an ethanol level of 180 in September show active drinking; he has a tremor today, CIWA and thiamine are not ordered, and coagulopathy (INR 1.7, fibrinogen 142, platelets 66) has no product plan.

asa.rationale: Decompensated cirrhosis with ascites, encephalopathy, varices, hyponatremia, coagulopathy.

decision.rationale: Rupture and strangulation risk outweigh deferral. Order CIWA monitoring and thiamine before dextrose, have plasma and platelets available or use viscoelastic testing, and tell the team about recent alcohol use.

redFlags.finding: Active alcohol use despite reported abstinence
redFlags.evidence: PEth 286 (08/2026); serum ethanol 180 on 09/12 ED fall; sister reports drinking since summer; tremor today.
redFlags.implication: Withdrawal (possibly delirium tremens) in the perioperative period; altered drug requirements.
redFlags.action: CIWA protocol, thiamine IV before glucose, plan for withdrawal treatment mindful of HE (dexmedetomidine or careful benzodiazepine).

redFlags.finding: Coagulopathy and thrombocytopenia without products ready
redFlags.evidence: INR 1.7, aPTT 38, fibrinogen 142, platelets 66; FFP and platelets not prepared.
redFlags.implication: Bleeding, though INR overstates risk in cirrhosis.
redFlags.action: TEG or ROTEM guided therapy; cryoprecipitate for low fibrinogen; platelets available; avoid volume overload from plasma.

redFlags.evidence: Ascites returning after 5 L LVP; distended abdomen.
redFlags.implication: Aspiration risk, reduced FRC, hypotension when abdomen opened.
redFlags.action: RSI, albumin for drained ascites, careful fluids.

redFlags.finding: Hepatic encephalopathy history and inconsistent lactulose
redFlags.evidence: Ammonia 64; slow responses; lactulose 'when I remember'.
redFlags.action: Minimize benzodiazepines and opioids, continue lactulose and rifaximin.
Avoid large saline loads and rapid correction.
Check Mg (1.6) and replete, choose antiemetics carefully.

redFlags.implication: Prolonged action of hepatically cleared drugs.
redFlags.action: Cisatracurium or rocuronium with sugammadex, short acting agents.

planItems.item: Arterial line to consider; glucose checks
Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision
2 units crossmatched; products by viscoelastic testing
Step down with hepatology and CIWA
